• Scientific evidence (Big Bang, evolution) contradicts a literal six-day creation. Most scientists accept the Earth is billions of years old, not thousands.

expect:
Arguments supporting the statement:
• St Paul wrote ‘If Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile’ (1 Corinthians 15:17). Without the resurrection, Christianity would have no foundation.
• The resurrection proves Jesus is the Son of God. Only God could conquer death, confirming Jesus’s divine nature.
• It gives Christians the promise of eternal life — ‘I am the resurrection and the life’ (John 11:25). Without this hope, the Christian message loses its power.
• It is the reason Christians worship on Sundays and celebrate Easter as their most important festival.
Arguments against the statement:
• The incarnation could be seen as more important — without God becoming human, none of the other events (crucifixion, resurrection) would have happened.
• The crucifixion is when salvation actually happened — Jesus’s death paid the price for sin. Without the sacrifice, the resurrection would have less meaning.
• Some Christians might argue that the teachings of Jesus are most important — the Sermon on the Mount and the parables guide how Christians live daily.
• Others argue that all the events are interconnected and equally important — you cannot separate incarnation, crucifixion, resurrection and ascension.

expect:
Arguments supporting the statement:
• James 2:17 states ‘Faith by itself, if it is not accompanied by action, is dead.’ This suggests that believing in God is not enough — Christians must also act on their beliefs.
• Catholics teach that good works are essential alongside faith. The sacraments (baptism, Eucharist) and acts of charity contribute to salvation.
• In the parable of the sheep and the goats (Matthew 25), those who helped the hungry, thirsty and sick were saved. This seems to prioritise actions over beliefs.
Arguments against the statement:
• Ephesians 2:8–9 states salvation is ‘by grace… through faith — not by works, so that no one can boast.’ Protestants argue salvation is a free gift that cannot be earned.
• The criminal crucified next to Jesus was promised paradise despite having no time for good works (Luke 23:43). This shows faith alone is sufficient.
• Martin Luther argued that humans are saved by faith alone (sola fide). Good works are a natural result of faith, not a condition for salvation.
• Some argue faith and works cannot be separated — genuine faith naturally produces good actions.

• The existence of saints and moral exemplars suggests some people come very close to sinless lives.
